# Sterling architecture & extension document (generated)

Sterling documents and extends itself by the same registry + checked-contract +
fail-loud discipline it imposes (§15). For every extensible set below: the
registry is the single source of truth, the named checks guard it, and the
"extending this" guidance is quoted from the set's owning feature article —
the durable store is authoritative; this file is a projection of it.

## Extensible set: record-types — Record types (durable knowledge shapes)  [state: active]

- Registry: packages/schemas/src/records.ts — RECORD_TYPES (schema + fts + fileKeys per member) + SYSTEM_REASONS/DRAIN_VERBS
- Checks: schemas registry test (1:1, unregistered rejected) + store write validation on every create

**Extending this:** One definition per shape, consumed by both the MCP server and the TUI (invariant 1); no raw path ever enters the store (invariant 2); for every extensible set the registry + its consistency check exist before members are added (invariant 3). Adding a record type or maintenance lane is a registry-member addition here, never a parallel definition elsewhere. Since 2026-07-17 (decision a0fc8743): featureArticleSchema + referenceMaterialSchema carry an optional working_tree symbolic name and config.ts a working_trees name→path map — detached-copy records resolve their file paths against their own tree, keeping machine-specific paths in config and repo-relative file_keys in records (invariant 2 holds).

## Extensible set: agents — Agents (the roster)  [state: active]

- Registry: agent-templates/registry.json (1:1 with templates)
- Checks: scripts/check-agent-registry.mjs, check-agent-prompts.mjs (§7.3 sections), check-spawn-contracts.mjs (§7.4), check-tool-grants.mjs (real tool names, both MCP prefixes, ToolSearch), check-skills.mjs (skill and command references), check-agents-visible.mjs (runtime)

**Extending this:** The roster divides judgment: the conductor orchestrates, the implementor and implementor-hard change code and tests, the researcher, scout and preflight read, the reviewer judges a finished diff, and the librarian applies store maintenance the conductor drafted. Skills are SOPs the conductor follows, and their file references are linted. Every template except the conductor carries one shared conduct rule (decision h19-subagentstart-front-porch-byte-budget-hazards-first-owner-pointers-no-overrun): when Sterling hook-delivered context is shown truncated with a persisted-file path, open that file before reasoning or acting; a brief or role contract still wins.

## Extensible set: hooks — Hooks (the knowledge loop at platform seams)  [state: active]

- Registry: hooks/hooks.json (project-level registrations)
- Checks: hooks.json emission check (forward-slash commands) + scripts/tests/hooks-full.test.mjs / enforcement.test.mjs

**Extending this:** Checkable rules are hooks, not prose (§6): every gate fires at the platform seam it guards, blocking gates fail closed, soft gates degrade loud through check_skipped — and because hooks are bundled standalone, the standalone launch path has nothing to repair. Hook-semantics drift can weaken a backstop, never a gate (the disposal gate lives in the script, not the hook). EXTENDING THE SUITE: a new hook is authored in scripts/hooks, bundled by build-hooks.mjs, and registered in EITHER hooks/hooks.json (to gate the conductor) or an agent's frontmatter (to scope it to that agent) — check-agent-registry enforces that every bundle is registered somewhere or carries a documented exception, so a bundled-but-unregistered hook cannot ship silently. Decide its posture explicitly: blocking means it must DENY when it cannot evaluate, soft means it must never block and must report what it skipped. Then place its description in the member article for its role (write gates, session guards, knowledge duty) rather than here — this article carries only what is true of the whole suite, so that touching one hook delivers that hook's group and not all twenty-four.

## Extensible set: toolchain-adapters — Toolchain adapters (per-stack capability layer)  [state: active]

- Registry: scripts/adapters/registry.json — name → module, fixed interface (capabilities/testPathGlobs/runCommands/runTests)
- Checks: checkAdapterRegistry() via scripts/check-agent-registry.mjs + adapter tests in scripts/tests/enforcement.test.mjs

**Extending this:** One classification authority per stack, declared not improvised: a new toolchain joins by registering an adapter module that exports the fixed interface, and every consumer derives from its declarations. A check whose required capability is absent degrades loud (recorded as check_skipped), never silently green (P5). Init warns once per absent optional capability at declaration time. TypeScript package tests are first-class: built from each owning package's tsconfig and run from dist (Node16 .js specifiers don't resolve from src), so a TS red/green check classifies on real assertions, never a false load-crash.
